title: Harvest and Room
premise: Orsen Nystrom, an urban explorer obsessed with documentation, inherits their grandmother's farmhouse and discovers a sealed cellar door leading to tunnels absent from every survey. The house's mirrors begin reflecting rooms one second late, and the lag grows — each second of delay marking another soul the house has 'counted.' Orsen learns their grandmother made a bargain: the family line feeds the house its dead in exchange for prosperity, and the count is coming due. To break it, Orsen must enter the reflected room itself, unmake the ledger of names written into the walls, and offer the house something it has never been given — a willing inheritance freely refused.
about_author: Ulyana Fairweather is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent a decade mapping abandoned infrastructure across the upper Midwest before turning to fiction. Their work explores what buildings remember and why families keep secrets in basements.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Arriving at the inherited farmhouse, Orsen photographs everything — a ritual of control — and notices the county plat map shows no cellar where one clearly exists. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity masked as professional detachment.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Sorting the estate, Orsen finds a handwritten ledger listing every family death with dates that don't match any official record — each entry annotated with a number counting down from 144. Beat: dread taking root beneath grief.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The bathroom mirror reflects Orsen's movements a full second behind. They film it; the footage shows nothing wrong. Documentation fails for the first time. Beat: the collapse of Orsen's core coping mechanism.

chapters.title: Sister of Glass
chapters.summary: POV Mara, Orsen's estranged sister, summoned by a cryptic voicemail. She arrives skeptical but catches her own reflection smiling when she isn't. Beat: reluctant alliance forming through shared disbelief.

chapters.title: The Sealed Door
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Behind the pantry, a brick arch mortared from the inside. Orsen's camera picks up sound through it: breathing, rhythmic, patient. Beat: the house stops being passive and becomes attentive.

chapters.title: Count to Fourteen
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A neighbor, old Mr. Halvorsen, warns them the Nystroms were 'keepers of the room' and that his own family lost two children to a lagging mirror in 1974. Beat: horror acquires local history and precedent.

chapters.title: What the Walls Are Owed
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. In grandmother's Bible, marginalia reveals the bargain: prosperity traded for deaths on schedule, the ledger a contract renewed each generation by a keeper. Beat: inheritance reframed as debt.

chapters.title: The Room Behind the Reflection
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The mirror-lag reaches three seconds; standing before the glass, Orsen sees the reflected room diverge — furniture rearranged, a figure seated in grandmother's chair. Beat: the boundary between reflection and place dissolving.

chapters.title: Mara's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Desperate to protect her daughter June, Mara secretly considers offering herself, believing the house takes only volunteers who understand the terms. Beat: love curdling into self-sacrifice as transaction.

chapters.title: Down Where the Survey Ends
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen breaks through the arch into tunnels that match their old urban-exploration photos exactly — photos taken years ago, miles away. The house has been mapping them back. Beat: the hunter realizes they were always the quarry.

chapters.title: Names in the Plaster
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Deep in the tunnel, walls are inscribed with every name from the ledger, each scratched out upon payment. Grandmother's name remains unscored — she never paid; she deferred. Beat: betrayal and terrible understanding.

chapters.title: June Counts to Ten
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Six-year-old June begins playing a counting game with her reflection, which answers. The lag around her accelerates unnaturally. Beat: parental terror at its sharpest pitch.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Last Warning
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Halvorsen, found dead in his truck outside the property, leaves a note: 'It counts what you owe, not what you give. Refuse it in writing.' Beat: hope arrives too late to be simple.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. A final letter from grandmother explains she cheated the house for forty years by substituting strangers — drifters, the missing — and the count now demands restitution with interest. Beat: moral vertigo; justice outside the law cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The lag hits ten seconds. Every mirror in the house reflects the tunnel instead of the rooms. The house is showing them where they'll be kept. Beat: claustrophobic inevitability.

chapters.title: Written Refusal
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Following Halvorsen's note, Mara drafts a formal renunciation of the inheritance for herself and June, but the ink dries gray and the words fade overnight. The house does not accept paperwork. Beat: legal language failing against older law.

chapters.title: Into the Reflection
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. At the twelfth second, Orsen steps through the hallway mirror deliberately, entering the reflected house — identical, silent, lit by no source. Beat: courage as a choice made while terrified.

chapters.title: The Counting Room
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. In the mirrored cellar, Orsen finds the original ledger grown into the wall like bone, and the thing that keeps count: a figure wearing grandmother's face, patiently waiting for balance. Beat: confrontation with the inherited self.

chapters.title: A Willing Inheritance, Refused
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen offers the house not a death but a choice: they will stay as keeper willingly if it releases all claims on the bloodline — then, once the ledger opens, they tear out their own page and refuse the office aloud. Beat: climax; freedom claimed through refusal rather than sacrifice.

chapters.title: Thirteen Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Mara. On the other side, the house convulses — mirrors crack in sequence like a countdown collapsing — and Mara pulls Orsen back through the shattering glass as the reflected house folds shut forever. Beat: rescue, reunion, raw relief.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Weeks later: the cellar is filled with concrete, the ledger burned, but Orsen keeps one cracked mirror shard — and checks it every morning, finding only a half-second of lag that never grows. Beat: wary peace, vigilance as new ritual.

chapters.title: Harvest and Room
chapters.summary: POV June. Years on, June finds the shard in a shoebox and, alone, holds it up. Her reflection smiles first — half a second early this time. Somewhere, something learned patience differently. Beat: quiet, unresolved dread; the harvest waits.
